tema: Pilot study comparing physiological responses to repeated exercise tests at 24 h in CFS, multiple sclerosis and controls.
diseno: Pilot study with 10 CFS patients, 7 with multiple sclerosis and 17 matched controls; maximal incremental cycle ergometer test on two days; HR, BP, RPE, VO2 and workload at anaerobic threshold and peak.
hallazgos: On day 2, CFS and MS had lower maximal workload than controls; CFS reduced workload (93 versus 132 W) and HR, whereas their controls improved. MS had lower workload on both days but improved on day 2.
conclusion: Exercise produces different responses in CFS and MS; the repeated test is valid for differentiating conditions with fatigue and workload could be the best indicator of PEM.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The conclusions add proposals (48-72 h protocols, submaximal test) and qualify that MS appeared less fit; small sample.

tema: Investigates the physiological timeline of PEM with repeated maximal tests at 48 and 72 h and the recovery time in ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 16 ME/CFS patients and 16 matched controls, randomly assigned to 48-h or 72-h protocols; repeated maximal incremental test; analysis at peak workload.
hallazgos: The 48-h ME/CFS group differed from controls in peak VO2 and workload on both tests, with a small, non-significant decrease; the 72-h group only on the second, and workload increased by about 10 W with no change in VO2. The 48-h group reported longer recovery.
conclusion: Recovery after repeated exercise is described (11 versus 5.5 days depending on the protocol), information relevant to exercise prescription and PEM management; chronotropic intolerance was observed in the 72-h group.
triangulacion: Abstract and discussion are consistent with the keywords (recovery, peak VO2). The discussion provides data absent from the abstract (chronotropic intolerance, recovery days) and contains acknowledgement noise.

tema: Clinical working definition, diagnostic and treatment protocols for ME/CFS (Canadian Consensus Criteria, Carruthers 2003).
diseno: Expert consensus document published in the Journal of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome; the available text is the cover and table of contents of the issue.
hallazgos: They are not stated in the available text; only authors and the contents of the issue appear (editorial on guidelines and the consensus document).
conclusion: Not stated for the consensus document; the conclusions text corresponds to another article in the same issue on Gulf War illness (chemical exposures, vaccines, infections).
triangulacion: No keywords; the abstract is ResearchGate opening text and the conclusions (discussion) come from a different article on the Gulf War, so the sources are neither consistent nor triangulable.

tema: Critically reviews the protocols and early data of the British IAPT programme applied to medically unexplained symptoms, specifically ME/CFS.
diseno: Critical review of treatment protocols and early data from the IAPT service; no own sample.
hallazgos: Identifies seven problems: unproven rationale, weak and disputed evidence base, promotional biases, exaggeration of recovery, under-reporting of dropouts and a significant risk of misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.
conclusion: Independent oversight is required; psychotherapy should not be the default option for unexplained symptoms and patients must be fully informed and receive adequate medical support.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions are more forceful: they add emerging evidence of neuroimmune disease, the unviability of the service and that the methods inflate recovery statistics.

tema: Comparative survey of ME/CFS patients in Italy, Latvia and the UK to guide policies that alleviate the burden of the disease.
diseno: Parallel patient surveys (88 Italy, 75 Latvia, 448 UK) with 95% CIs, and a questionnaire to 91 general practitioners in Latvia.
hallazgos: Demographics, impact on household income and quality of life were similar between countries; there were differences in progression and management, social care and social attitudes. GET as practised in the UK proved universally ineffective.
conclusion: There are similarities in impact and difficulty speaking with doctors, and differences in care and attitudes; shared international protocols and more research on needs are required.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions add the need for international protocols and care pathways. The survey of Latvian doctors is not reflected in the keywords.

tema: Analyses the relationship between stigma and functional capacity in ME/CFS and compares it with other neurological diseases.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with a convenience sample of 206 people with ME/CFS; standardized self-reported measures of stigma, health and social participation, compared with published data from three neurological conditions.
hallazgos: Stigma correlated significantly with all health and function measures (r from -0.30 to -0.42). The ME/CFS sample reported more stigma (d = 1.30) and worse health (d = 1.86-2.16) and functioning (d = 1.63).
conclusion: People with ME/CFS report more stigma than other conditions, associated with functional capacity; clinicians should consider stigma and act to reduce judgement.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources. The PDF conclusions extend the explanation of stigma to functional limitations and add a clinical recommendation absent from the abstract.

tema: Describes three patients with severe ME/CFS whose symptoms improved after the diagnosis and surgical treatment of cervical canal stenosis.
diseno: Series of three consecutive cases with ME/CFS and orthostatic intolerance; function assessed with the Karnofsky scale and the SF-36 physical function subscale before and after surgery.
hallazgos: Hyperreflexia (2 of 3), Hoffman sign (2 of 3), tremor (2 of 3) and absent gag reflex (1 of 3) were observed, with a canal diameter of 6-8.5 mm. Anterior cervical surgery (disc prosthesis or hybrid technique) was associated with improvement of myelopathic symptoms, resolution of dizziness and haemodynamic dysfunction, and overall improvement of ME/CFS.
conclusion: Cervical stenosis would have contributed to the pathogenesis of refractory ME/CFS and orthostatic symptoms; myelopathic signs should be carefully sought in severe patients who do not respond to treatment.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions specify that they were young women refractory to medical and psychiatric management. The causal inference is based on only three cases.

tema: Validates the two-day CPET in men with ME/CFS and compares their response with that described in women.
diseno: Study with 25 men with ME/CFS (of 77 evaluated) who met the protocol criteria; VO2, HR, BP, workload and RER at peak and ventilatory threshold; paired Student's t.
hallazgos: Mean age 44 years, BMI 27.1 and median duration of 10 years. Resting HR and BP and RER did not change; VO2 and workload at peak and ventilatory threshold decreased significantly on the second test.
conclusion: Men with ME/CFS show, like women, a reduction in exercise capacity on consecutive CPET; the test can be used in research and in applications for social benefits.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the abstract is partially truncated in results. The conclusions add the medico-legal use and the need to compare by severity and comorbidities.

tema: Audit of the knowledge and experience of ME among UK hospital doctors.
diseno: Questionnaire audit of 44 doctors attending a training event; proportions, 95% CIs and Fisher's exact test.
hallazgos: Few had formal training on ME and few knew how to diagnose it; most lacked confidence in its management. 82% believed that ME was at least partly psychological; knowledge about definitions, diagnosis, management and impact was very poor.
conclusion: Most doctors lack training and experience in ME; prioritizing up-to-date medical education at undergraduate and postgraduate level and repeating the audit are recommended.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions come from the abstract, with no independent source. The keywords include 'psychological factors', reflecting the doctors' beliefs rather than a focus of the study.

tema: EUROMENE expert consensus on diagnosis, service provision and care of people with ME/CFS in Europe.
diseno: Consensus of clinicians and researchers from 22 countries and 55 European professionals, informed by patients (COST action 15111, 2016-2020).
hallazgos: Evaluates knowledge and experience on healthcare for ME/CFS in Europe and formulates recommendations; the specific recommendations are not stated in the available text.
conclusion: Not stated in the available text.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (diagnosis, services, guidelines); the extracted conclusions are only noise (data availability, funding and conflicts of interest), so they do not allow triangulation.

tema: Investigates whether low-dose naltrexone (LDN) restores TRPM3 channel function in NK cells of ME/CFS patients.
diseno: In vitro study with 9 ME/CFS patients on LDN treatment and 9 age- and sex-matched controls; whole-cell patch-clamp technique with pregnenolone sulphate (agonist) and ononetin (antagonist).
hallazgos: In NK cells from patients on LDN, TRPM3-type ionic currents with outward rectification were recorded after pregnenolone sulphate, significantly modulated by ononetin, indicating restoration of TRPM3 activity.
conclusion: LDN could have therapeutic potential in ME/CFS through mechanisms involving TRPM3 and opioid receptors in NK cells, which supports prospective randomized clinical trials on its role and dose.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion agree; the discussion (with noise from funding and ethics) adds that the wide distribution of TRPM3 could explain symptoms, although the sample is small and there is no clinical evaluation.

tema: Literature review on the knowledge and understanding of ME/CFS among general practitioners.
diseno: MEDLINE search and synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM); 33 quantitative and qualitative articles classified by focus.
hallazgos: Between a third and a half of general practitioners do not accept ME/CFS as a clinical entity or do not feel confident diagnosing and managing it; a similar proportion of patients is dissatisfied with primary care. The findings have barely changed in decades.
conclusion: Lack of knowledge is widespread and the resulting diagnostic delay is a risk factor for severe and prolonged illness, making it difficult to estimate prevalence and economic impact.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources; the PDF conclusions add the geographic consistency of the findings and the likely increase in costs.

tema: Systematic review comparing the clinical presentation and symptoms of long COVID with those of ME/CFS.
diseno: Search in MEDLINE and PsycInfo up to January 2021 according to PRISMA; 21 studies included in qualitative analysis compared with a list of 29 ME/CFS symptoms.
hallazgos: 25 of the 29 known ME/CFS symptoms were reported in at least one long COVID study.
conclusion: There is great clinical overlap between long COVID and ME/CFS; post-COVID follow-up and treatment and a more standardized research methodology are needed.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions highlight the pioneering nature of the study and the future importance of investigating both conditions together.

tema: Explores the impact of ME/CFS on the quality of life of patients and their relatives.
diseno: Quantitative study with postal questionnaires; 24 adult patients (WHOQOL-BREF) and 42 relatives (FROM-16).
hallazgos: Quality of life very reduced in patients, especially in physical health (median 19); relatives showed emotional and personal-social impact (FROM-16 total 20.5). There was a significant correlation between the patient's quality of life and that of their relatives.
conclusion: Having an adult relative with ME/CFS has a great impact on the partner and family; it is advisable to measure it in consultation and to ensure support for relatives.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources. The PDF conclusions are more cautious, acknowledging that it is a small exploratory study that justifies larger-scale research.

tema: Re-examines the 1955 Royal Free Hospital outbreak to assess whether it was an infectious disease or epidemic hysteria.
diseno: Collection of testimonies by telephone interview and letters from 27 former hospital workers (6 developed ME), contrasted with the paper on the hysteria hypothesis and the original medical reports.
hallazgos: The accounts describe an infectious illness that affected the lymphatic, muscular and nervous systems, not compatible with epidemic hysteria; some of McEvedy and Beard's data are contradictory or of doubtful validity.
conclusion: The 1955 outbreak was an organic infectious disease and not psychogenic epidemic hysteria; the authors maintain that ME/CFS is an organic disease.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions extend the claim from the specific outbreak to all of ME/CFS, a broader generalization than the abstract allows.

tema: Investigates whether ME/CFS patients in Germany are medically underserved and validates the German version of the DSQ-SF.
diseno: Online survey of 499 participants meeting Canadian Consensus Criteria and PEM of 14 h or more; psychometric analysis of the DSQ-SF against the SF-36.
hallazgos: Participants reported geographic and economic barriers to using services and low satisfaction with the most consulted doctor. The German DSQ-SF showed good reliability, single-factor structure and construct validity.
conclusion: ME/CFS patients in Germany are medically underserved; the German DSQ-SF is a brief, reliable and valid instrument.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources; the PDF conclusions add the need for medical training and specialized care.

tema: Explores the teaching of ME/CFS in UK medical schools.
diseno: Survey of the 34 UK medical schools (2018-2019 academic year), with 22 responses (65%).
hallazgos: 13 of 22 (59%) taught ME/CFS, mostly in lectures delivered from ten specialties; seven included it in exams and three reported probable clinical exposure. Two thirds wanted more materials; none shared their syllabus.
conclusion: Training is inadequate and has not progressed in two decades; the GMC and MSC are urged to change curricula and to consider a specialty covering ME/CFS, post-viral fatigue and long COVID.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions add the need to set aside discrepant beliefs about pathogenesis and to believe the patient; the new specialty proposal appears only in the abstract.

tema: Gathers the perception of European experts on knowledge of ME/CFS among primary care doctors.
diseno: Survey of EUROMENE members; 23 responses from 19 countries (95% response per country); descriptive and thematic analysis of free text.
hallazgos: Serious concern about the knowledge of general practitioners; an estimated 60% of patients remain undiagnosed. Lack of confidence, disbelief and widespread erroneous attributions, and a shortage of specialized centres were perceived.
conclusion: Lack of knowledge in primary care is a main cause of missed or late diagnoses, makes it difficult to estimate incidence, prevalence and economic impact and increases the burden from poor initial management.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions insist on the lack of specialized centres and on the need to survey doctors directly, acknowledging that these are experts' perceptions.

tema: Analyses the scope for preventive programmes for ME/CFS and their possible economic benefits in Europe.
diseno: Report/narrative review from the EUROMENE socioeconomic group; no new data.
hallazgos: There is little scope for primary prevention because of the scarcity of modifiable risk factors, except for exposure to agricultural organophosphates. Secondary prevention offers greater scope by reducing the diagnostic delay associated with greater severity and cost.
conclusion: Secondary prevention through early detection and diagnosis is the most promising strategy; more research on risk factors, particularly occupational ones, is needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree fully; the conclusions from the discussion are almost all noise (contributions, funding), apart from a mention of improving orthostatic intolerance.

tema: Systematic review of mind-body interventions for treating ME/CFS symptoms.
diseno: Search in MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Cochrane CENTRAL up to September 2020; 12 of 382 references included (7 RCTs, the rest single-arm); descriptive synthesis.
hallazgos: Interventions: MBSR, MBCT, relaxation, qigong, cognitive-behavioural stress management, ACT and isometric yoga. Fatigue improved in nine studies, anxiety/depression in eight and quality of life in three.
conclusion: Mind-body interventions improved fatigue, anxiety/depression and functioning, but small samples, heterogeneous criteria and high risk of bias limit the result.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions add that no study measured PEM as a central outcome, a critical nuance absent from the abstract.

tema: Editorial presenting a special issue on ME/CFS: nature of the disease, medical disbelief, family impact, COVID-19 and guidelines.
diseno: Editorial/narrative review of the articles in the collection; no own data.
hallazgos: Summarizes the growing knowledge of the pathology, new organizations (Doctors with ME, US ME/CFS Clinical Coalition, EUROMENE), the overlap with COVID-19 and proposes the category PAPIS (post-active phase of infection syndromes). Contextualizes the difficulties with the NICE guideline.
conclusion: The mistakes of the past have had an immense impact on patients and families, but research offers real prospects of progress; care must be person-centred and early detection is key.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree (NICE, COVID-19, family impact); the conclusions from the discussion, with final noise, have a more evaluative and hopeful tone than the abstract.

tema: Compares the antibody response to mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection and the reactivation of latent viruses in ME/CFS patients and healthy donors.
diseno: Case-control study with 95 ME/CFS patients and 110 unvaccinated healthy donors; multiplex soluble immunoassay in plasma and saliva for anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies and antibody fingerprints against HSV1, HSV2, VZV, EBV, CMV, HHV6 and HERV-K.
hallazgos: At 3-6 months after infection, salivary antibodies indicated strong reactivation of EBV, HHV6 and HERV-K in both cohorts, but more intense in ME/CFS; anti-EBNA1 IgG rose only in patients and anti-VCA IgG was already higher before infection.
conclusion: ME/CFS shows an altered and chronically activated antiviral profile against latent viruses, and mild SARS-CoV-2 infection is a potent trigger of reactivation detectable locally in saliva, not in plasma.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the abstract) are consistent and the conclusion is identical to that of the abstract, so there is no independent source to qualify it.

tema: Studies whether herpesvirus DNA loads in saliva are related to the phenotype and severity of ME/CFS.
diseno: Longitudinal study with 30 ME/CFS patients (saliva monthly for 6 months and during exacerbations) and 14 healthy controls; droplet digital PCR for the nine human herpesviruses and symptom questionnaires.
hallazgos: HHV-6B, HHV-7, HSV-1 and EBV were detected, with HHV-6B and HHV-7 loads higher in patients. One group showed fluctuating patterns, in which loads correlated positively with pain, neurocognition and autonomic dysfunction; another showed a stable presentation.
conclusion: Fluctuating viral load, linked to the herpesviral reactivation state, could be involved in pathogenesis or be a consequence of immune dysfunction; the tools developed allow large-scale epidemiological studies.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the discussion only provides the idea that cause or effect remains to be determined, along with ethics and funding noise, which agrees with the causal ambiguity of the abstract.

tema: Reviews scientific advances and the clinical approach to small fibre polyneuropathy.
diseno: Clinical narrative review; no own sample.
hallazgos: Confirmation with skin biopsy (epidermal neurite density with PGP9.5) and autonomic testing is recommended. A meta-analysis attributes 49% of cases labelled fibromyalgia to small fibre neuropathy; treatable causes are identified in a third to a half of patients, and small fibre dysfunction could contribute to PEM, POTS and gastrointestinal symptoms.
conclusion: Since small fibres regenerate, treating the causes can allow recovery; the prognosis is usually hopeful, especially in young people, and better clinical and public education is needed.
triangulacion: High coherence among keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions; the latter add B cell autoreactivity and the need for simpler diagnostic metrics. ME/CFS does not appear as an explicit focus.

tema: Looks for serum antibodies against neuronal proteins in ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control study with coded sera from 50 patients and 50 healthy individuals; screening on brain tissue and neuronal cultures, antigen-specific cell assays and radioimmunoassays, and association with clinical data.
hallazgos: Eight patients and 11 controls showed some immunoreactivity against neuronal or neuromuscular junction proteins, but only 1 patient and 2 controls had specific antibodies; in patients, seropositivity was associated with shorter duration and greater severity.
conclusion: There is no higher frequency of anti-neuronal antibodies nor a specific causal antibody in ME/CFS, although the association with recent and severe illness suggests a possible role in onset in some patients.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more cautious, noting the low intensity of binding and that these low-level antibodies would require other factors to be pathogenic.
